Desk Talk
We are currently going through the third distinct phase of Middle East exports since the Hormuz crisis began. After suffering an immediate loss of around 15 mb/d of export capacity in the spring months and then experiencing the short-lived reopening during the second half of July, we are now in a phase of increased tanker shuttling, which has become very prominent since early August with volumes estimated to have reached ~4.5 mb/d. Middle Eastern producers, along with a handful of risk-tolerant tanker operators, have moved cargoes through the Strait of Hormuz to Ship-To-Ship hubs off Oman and Fujairah, where the volumes are transferred onto other tankers for onward delivery.
